features.name: argument_has_apology_phrase
features.definition: Does the OP's argument text contain at least one explicit polite apology phrase?
features.spec: Read df['argument'] only. If missing or not a string, return null. Otherwise lowercase the text and return 1 if it matches regex r"\b(i'?m sorry|i am sorry|sorry for|sorry if|sorry about|sorry to|my apologies|apologies|apologi[sz]e|apologi[sz]ing|apology|pardon me|excuse me|forgive me)\b" else 0. Empty string returns 0. Raw literal matching, no semantic filtering.

h0: Discussions whose argument has argument_has_apology_phrase = 1 have the same likelihood of view change as those with argument_has_apology_phrase = 0.
h1: Discussions whose argument has argument_has_apology_phrase = 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than those with argument_has_apology_phrase = 0.
note: Operational assumption: "explicit polite apology phrases" is operationalized as a fixed literal phrase list (sorry/apologize/my apologies/pardon/excuse me/forgive me); it may include non-apologetic uses (e.g., "sorry state") and miss unlisted phrasings. Uses current argument text, which may include edits and outcome announcements; raw matching is not outcome-free or pre-outcome. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.
